guidance_diff.why: The last two 8-K Exhibit 99.1 press releases for this name have not been pulled from EDGAR, so there is no mechanical guidance diff. This is the free substitute for a transcript: it carries the guidance figures and none of the questions.
guidance_diff.caveat: Mechanical. Two press releases, sentences with a forward-looking word and a figure, matched on metric and period. It does not read tone, it cannot see a guide given without a number, and a filer that changes how it names a period between releases shows one lapsed and one introduced where a reader would see one reiterated. The verbatim sentence sits under every row so the machine's reading can be checked.

earnings_text.text: Q2 2026 (July 30, 2026): revenue $4.3 billion up 17%, non-GAAP EPS $14.29 up 11%, Dupixent up 38% constant currency, US Dupixent $4.6 billion up 42%, Eylea HD US $596 million up 52%, legacy Eylea $412 million down 45%. Management expects legacy Eylea demand to keep falling low to mid teens sequentially. Q1 2026 was the first of the two double digit quarters.

read.prior_quarter_label: Q1 2026 — named but not detailed; the note gives no date and no figures for it
read.headline: Revenue grew 17% to $4.3 billion on a second straight double-digit quarter, and the only forward-looking statement in the note is a decline guide: management expects legacy Eylea demand to keep falling low to mid teens sequentially.

guidance.detail: The note records exactly one forward-looking management statement for the quarter: legacy Eylea demand is expected to keep falling low to mid teens sequentially. It follows a reported legacy Eylea quarter of $412 million, down 45%. The note gives no time horizon, no absolute floor, no prior guide to compare against, and no indication of whether this expectation is new, reiterated or revised — so raised/cut/maintained cannot be scored.
guidance.quote: Management expects legacy Eylea demand to keep falling low to mid teens sequentially.

tone.assessment: Not determinable. The note attributes no tone, adjective, or framing to management. It contains a single paraphrased management sentence and no direct quotes, no speaker names, and no call commentary. The one observation available is compositional rather than tonal: the sole statement credited to management concerns a declining product line, while every growth figure in the earnings section is reported without any management attribution.
tone.evidence: Management expects legacy Eylea demand to keep falling low to mid teens sequentially.
tone.confidence: low — and it cannot be higher, because the note carries no direct quotation of management at all. The IR release and the Motley Fool transcript are listed in Sources but never excerpted, so no tonal evidence reaches the audited file. Any read of posture would be imported, not extracted.

read.market_reaction: Not given for this quarter. The note contains no post-earnings price move, no volume, and no analyst response to the July 30 print. Its only market data is a screen line dated more than five weeks later: "Price 843.47 USD on 2026-09-04", with the stock "-1% from 52 week high, -29% from all time high" and "Forward P/E 13.9 vs own 4 year median 18.7". The note also records "Next fiscal year EPS estimate moved +4.7% in 90 days" and short interest of 2.5% of float. All of it is labelled screen data pulled 2026-09-04 and is never linked by the note to the earnings report, so it cannot be read as a reaction to it.

new_risks.risk: The legacy Eylea decline is guided to continue, not stabilize. The quarter already reported legacy Eylea at $412 million, down 45%, and management expects demand to keep falling at a low-to-mid-teens sequential rate from there.
new_risks.quote: Management expects legacy Eylea demand to keep falling low to mid teens sequentially.

dodged.topic: Eylea HD's sequential trajectory — the precise variable the note's own thesis killer keys on
dodged.reasoning: The note's stated thesis killer is "Eylea HD sales down sequentially for two quarters". But every Eylea HD figure in the file is a growth rate against an unnamed base: "Eylea HD US $596 million up 52%" in the earnings section and "up 52% to $596 million in the US" in Business quality. Meanwhile the single forward statement credited to management covers legacy Eylea, not HD. The note thus provides no way to check its own tripwire, and gives no sign that HD's sequential path was addressed. Whether management discussed it and the note dropped it, or it was never addressed, cannot be told from this file.

dodged.topic: The pipeline — absent from the earnings section entirely
dodged.reasoning: The note's own description of the company includes "a deep pipeline and a genetics research engine", and the bear case flags that "The pipeline has had failures". Yet the Q2 paragraph carries only revenue, non-GAAP EPS, four product line items (Dupixent constant-currency growth, US Dupixent, Eylea HD US, legacy Eylea) and the one legacy Eylea expectation. No trial, readout, approval, or program is named anywhere in the file. Caveat: this is a one-paragraph summary of a quarter, so its silence is weak evidence about what was actually said on the call.

dodged.topic: What share of Dupixent economics accrues to Regeneron
dodged.reasoning: The bear case states that "Sanofi takes a large share of it", but the note never quantifies that share anywhere. The earnings section reports "Dupixent up 38% constant currency" and "US Dupixent $4.6 billion up 42%" with no accompanying statement about the split, and the file offers no mechanism, no percentage, and no reconciliation. Same caveat: the note is a summary, so absence here is not proof management avoided it.

The note names pricing as a standing risk twice — "drug pricing politics are a permanent overhang" in the bear case, and the thesis killer "a pricing law that hits Dupixent specifically" — yet the earnings section contains no pricing, policy, reimbursement, or net-price item of any kind. Weak-evidence caveat applies.

not_determinable: The comparison basis for every Q2 growth rate. The note writes bare "up 17%", "up 11%", "up 42%", "up 52%" and "down 45%" and never labels any of them year-over-year or sequential. The only basis the file ever names is "sequentially", and only for the legacy Eylea expectation. Reading the Q2 rates as year-over-year would be imported convention, not text.

Anything about Q1 2026 beyond a single clause. The note says only "Q1 2026 was the first of the two double digit quarters" — no revenue, no EPS, no product figures — so no sequential comparison and no quarter-on-quarter change can be computed for any line.
Whether guidance was raised, cut, maintained, introduced or withdrawn. The note records no prior guidance of any kind, so the legacy Eylea expectation cannot be scored against a previous one.

How US Dupixent sales of $4.6 billion relate to total company revenue of $4.3 billion. The note prints both figures in the same sentence and never reconciles them, never states who books what, and never labels either figure's basis.

Whether the "$6 billion of quarterly global sales across nine indications" figure in Business quality refers to Q2 2026 or to some other quarter. It carries no quarter label and no date, so it cannot be tied to the reported period or compared with the $4.6 billion US figure.

Whether the quarter beat or missed expectations. The note contains no consensus, no estimate-versus-actual comparison, and no beat/miss language. The only estimate reference in the file is a screen line: "Next fiscal year EPS estimate moved +4.7% in 90 days".
The stock's reaction to the July 30 print. The only price in the note is dated more than five weeks later — "Price 843.47 USD on 2026-09-04" — and is labelled screen data, not a response to earnings.

Ex-US performance. Both product revenue figures in the earnings section are explicitly US-only ("US Dupixent", "Eylea HD US"); no rest-of-world figure, no geographic split, and no global product total for the quarter is given.

Any quarterly margin, cash flow, share count, or balance sheet figure. The financial table stops at FY2025 and the Q2 paragraph carries only revenue and non-GAAP EPS. The note's balance sheet comment ("Net cash balance sheet") is undated.

Anything management said in its own words. The file carries no direct quote, no speaker name, and no Q&A content. The IR release and the Motley Fool transcript are listed as sources but never excerpted.
Any product beyond Dupixent and Eylea. Those two are the only products named anywhere in the file; there is no other franchise, segment, or launch to assess.
Capital allocation for the quarter. No buyback, dividend, M&A, or business development item appears anywhere in the note.

The combined Eylea franchise number for the quarter. The note gives Eylea HD US ($596 million) and legacy Eylea ($412 million) separately, but never a franchise total, and never states whether the legacy figure is US-only or global — so the two are not safely additive.
Whether Eylea HD is growing or shrinking sequentially, in dollars or percent. Only a growth rate against an unstated base is provided.
How many of the nine Dupixent indications contributed to the quarter, or when the ninth was added. The indication count appears only in the undated Business quality line.
Any operating detail behind the 17% revenue growth — pricing versus volume, inventory, one-time items, or currency (beyond the single "constant currency" tag on Dupixent growth).

thesis.why_on_the_list: Compounder bucket, rank 69. Forward P/E 13.9 vs an 18.7 median, 29% off its high. Two straight quarters of double digit growth on both lines while the market fixates on Eylea biosimilars.
thesis.business_quality: Dupixent is one of the largest drugs in the world and still growing 38%: $6 billion of quarterly global sales across nine indications. Eylea HD is converting the base (up 52% to $596 million in the US) while legacy Eylea declines 45% to biosimilars. Net cash balance sheet. Science driven management with a long record.
thesis.verdict: Buy now, September tranche. Buy zone $770 to $880. Conviction 4 of 5.

logged.thesis: Dupixent up 38% and Eylea HD up 52% offset legacy Eylea erosion; two straight double digit quarters at 13.9x forward. Net cash.
logged.wrong_if: Dupixent growth under 15%, Eylea HD down sequentially twice, or a close under $650.

risks.bear_case: Eylea was half the company two years ago and it is being eaten by biosimilars faster than HD can replace it. Dupixent growth will decelerate from 38% as indications mature, and Sanofi takes a large share of it. The pipeline has had failures and drug pricing politics are a permanent overhang.
killers: Dupixent growth under 15%, Eylea HD sales down sequentially for two quarters, or a pricing law that hits Dupixent specifically

multiples.label: Forward P/E
multiples.basis_note: The two sides are not the same multiple. The left is a forward P/E, the Street's estimate of next year's earnings. The median on the right is trailing: the price at each fiscal year end divided by that year's reported diluted EPS. Where earnings are expected to grow, forward is mechanically lower than trailing, so this column reads cheap by construction.

multiples.label: EV/EBITDA
multiples.basis_note: Both sides are trailing, so this comparison is like for like.

own_history.caveat: The median is taken at 4 fiscal year ends, so it is a 4-point median. That is a thin basis for 'cheap against its own history' and it says nothing about whether the old multiple was deserved.
own_history.basis_warning: Read the P/E row with care. Across the 136 names that carry both comparisons, 85% print a negative 'vs median' on forward P/E with a median of -29%, against 50% and 0.0% on EV/EBITDA where both sides are trailing. That gap is the basis mismatch, not 136 companies being cheap. It is also correlated with growth: faster-growing names look cheaper here (rank correlation -0.28 against revenue CAGR, versus -0.15 for EV/EBITDA), because their forward earnings are further above their trailing ones. The score weights the like-for-like EV/EBITDA comparison more heavily for exactly this reason.

drawdown.caveat: The all-time high is the highest closing price; the 52-week high is an intraday high. They are not on the same basis, and the drawdown from the all-time high is therefore understated.

price_basis.note: The drawdowns and the multiple-versus-median above were computed inside the price screen from its own last close, which is not quite the price shown at the top of this page: the two come from different passes of the pipeline and differ by a fraction of a percent. Neither is wrong; they are just not the same number.
